newsitem.title: UK: Traders surprised over Brazil stand on coffee meet.
newsitem.headline: Traders surprised over Brazil stand on coffee meet.

text.p: Coffee markets showed little reaction to news Brazil failed to declare its stand on an African lobby for further cuts in world coffee exports in the first half of 1997.
But London traders voiced surprise that Brazil supported a request by African producers to hold an extraordinary meeting of the Assoiciation of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).

"It's a surprise they actually asked for a meeting because yesterday they said they did not think much of the idea," said one trader. "I think they are going to find it tough to get it through," he said.
"Even if the Brazilians agree with it, and they have got to have the Brazilians as they are the biggest producers, I think the Indonesians are not going to allow the idea (of cuts) as well," he said.

Colombia, Ivory Coast and Uganda had agreed on a need to increase the amount of coffee witheld under the Association of Coffee Producing Countries' export programme during the first half of 1997 by about 2.5 million 60-kg bags.

Broker GNI in its daily commentary earlier on Friday said: "Still it remains within the realms of possibility that further progress could be made in this plan, but Brazil will only give its backing if it feels it will give a definite boost to export revenue."
